name: Marshall Islands
system_note: The president is elected by parliament.
snapshot: A US-allied atoll nation still living with the legacy of 67 American nuclear tests, which renewed its compact with Washington in 2024.
culture: Marshallese navigators used stick charts made of palm ribs and shells to map ocean swells, a famous piece of traditional knowledge. Clan and land rights pass through the mother's line. Church, singing and family gatherings are central to life.
society: The US tested 67 nuclear weapons at Bikini and Enewetak between 1946 and 1958, and radioactive waste remains in a leaking dome on Runit Island. Under a Compact of Free Association, the US provides aid and defence, and Marshallese can live and work in America; a large community lives in Arkansas. Rising seas threaten Majuro.
situation: Hilda Heine was elected president again by parliament in January 2024. The Marshall Islands recognises Taiwan, and its renewed US compact secured new funding over 20 years.
power: A parliamentary system: the 33-seat Nitijela elects the president, who is both head of state and head of government.
